question.problem:
An amusement park knows that $25%$ of its visitors ride the rollercoaster. The manager of the park conducts a random sample of $125$ visitors. Find a normal approximation for the probability that fewer than $40$ of them rode the rollercoaster. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=125,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.25.$

Now, since

$$
np=125(0.25)=31.25>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=125(1-0.25)=93.75>5,
$$

and $n=125$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.25,\frac{0.25(1-0.25)}{125}) \\  & ∼N(0.25,0.0015).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If fewer than $40$ visitors in the sample rode the rollercoaster, then 

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}<\frac{40}{125}=0.32.
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.32).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}>0.4) & =P(Z<\frac{0.32-0.25}{\sqrt{0.0015}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<1.81) \\  & =Φ(1.81).\end{aligned}
$$
